failure_summary.description: Calls omitted or misrepresented requested sort, locale, unit, query, casing, or string-versus-number values.
Some calls used the provider's descriptive text instead of the exact provider-and-API endpoint name.
A broad endpoint was treated as covering every facet, omitting a dedicated current-conditions or general-details call.
The agent called several equivalent validation tools for each email rather than selecting one suitable endpoint.
Some outputs omitted empty parameter arrays or failed to serialize parameter entries as name/value objects.

patch.reasoning: Clarify how to construct endpoint names from tool listings, distinguish separate requested facets from duplicate calls, and make explicit sort and regional-locale mappings more operational. The existing schema and response-format rules already cover general serialization and array requirements, so those are not repeated.

edits.target: Choose the most directly fitting documented endpoint using its exact `Provider: endpoint` name.
edits.content: Construct that name from the short provider label and the endpoint name shown under `API`, formatted `Provider: API`. Omit descriptive or marketing text following the provider label; do not use it as part of the tool name.

edits.target: For a broad request, prefer a documented broad or all-scope endpoint when it fully provides the requested output; do not choose a narrower endpoint merely because it has fewer required arguments. Conversely, cover separately requested outputs when they require distinct endpoints rather than assuming one broad or multi-capability lookup covers every facet.
edits.content: For a single broad deliverable, prefer a documented broad or all-scope endpoint when it fully provides the requested output. For explicitly distinct deliverables, check coverage facet by facet and use a direct endpoint for each requested facet when available, even if another endpoint returns overlapping information; include a general-details endpoint when general details are requested in addition to named facets. Use only one best-fitting endpoint for a given subject and facet—do not call equivalent validators or searches merely to increase confidence.

edits.target: When a request specifies a market or locale, populate directly corresponding documented parameters (such as country, store, currency, or language) when their values are documented or unambiguously implied; use canonical codes and a market-specific locale when a documented mapping establishes one.
edits.content: When both a market and language are specified and the endpoint accepts a regional language tag, use the established combined locale (for example, `en-US` rather than `en`) and apply it to each requested endpoint that supports that field. Do not add a language or locale that the request and documented mapping do not support.

edits.target: If the user explicitly requests default sorting and the endpoint exposes a documented default-sort value, use that value; do not guess or add unrelated parameters.
edits.content: Also map named sort intent to the exact documented token (for example, “most relevant” to `RELEVANCE` when that enum is listed). Do not omit a requested sort merely because the sort parameter is optional.
